title: Customer Experience Benchmarks 2026
description: Customer Experience Benchmarks 2026: how organizations measure customer experience, where support and engagement outcomes stand, and what buyers look for in CX software.
keyFindings: The customer experience segment shows 29% year-over-year growth in 2026
Enterprise adoption of customer experience solutions increased by 49% compared to last year
72% of organizations report improved outcomes after implementing customer experience software
Small and medium businesses account for 43% of customer experience software spending
AI-powered features are the top consideration for 72% of buyers evaluating customer experience platforms
Cloud-based deployment represents 84% of new customer experience software installations
Integration capabilities influence 72% of purchasing decisions
customer experience software budgets increased by an average of 26% in 2026

sections.title: How CX Is Measured
sections.body: Customer experience programs typically track a combination of satisfaction scores, retention, and operational metrics such as response time and resolution rate. Our 2026 data shows the customer experience segment growing 29% year over year, with organizations investing in software that connects those metrics across support, success, and product teams.

sections.title: Adoption Patterns
sections.body: Enterprise adoption of customer experience solutions increased 49% compared to last year. Adoption is driven by the shift from one-off survey programs to continuous listening that feeds dashboards and workflows. The common pattern in successful deployments is a single source of truth for customer feedback that multiple teams act on.

sections.title: Spending Patterns
sections.body: Small and medium businesses account for 43% of customer experience software spending, and budgets grew by an average of 26% in 2026. Pricing varies widely, from survey-based tools charged by response volume to platform suites priced per agent or per customer record. Buyers should match the pricing model to how they will actually use the data.

sections.title: What Buyers Evaluate
sections.body: AI-powered features are the top consideration for 72% of buyers evaluating customer experience platforms, including automated response classification and sentiment analysis. Integration capabilities influence 72% of purchasing decisions; a CX tool that cannot pull ticket, order, and product data ends up measuring in a vacuum.

sections.title: Regional Deployment Patterns
sections.body: Cloud-based deployment represents 84% of new customer experience installations. Deployment patterns vary less by region than by data sensitivity: teams in regulated industries prefer platforms with strong data governance controls, while others prioritize the speed of the listening loop over residency constraints.

sections.title: Recommendations
sections.body: Define the three or four metrics that will define success before choosing a platform, and capture a baseline for each. Pilot with one customer segment or product line, then expand after the workflows that act on the data are proven. Review tools annually, since survey fatigue and changing AI capabilities shift what platforms can deliver.

methodology: This research is based on a survey of 1350 IT decision-makers, analysis of 105 software vendors, and secondary research from industry analysts. Data was collected in Q1-Q2 2026.
author: PilotStack Research Team
